source.text: וְלִבְנֵ֣י יִשָׂשכָ֗ר תּוֹלָ֧ע וּפוּאָ֛ה יָשׁ֥וּב וְשִׁמְר֖וֹן אַרְבָּעָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] sons of Issachar: Tola and Puah, Jashub and Shimron, four.

en.L: And [as] for the sons of Issachar: Tola and Puah, Jashub and Shimron, four.
en.B: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron, four in all.
en.R: Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron.

decisions.choice: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron: Issachar's four sons, as in Genesis 46:13 and Numbers 26:23-24
decisions.reason: Genesis 46:13 spells the second son Puvah and calls the third Iob; Numbers 26:24 calls him Jashub, as here. The chapter now turns to the tribes north of Judah, starting with Issachar.

decisions.choice: Jashub, as the Hebrew text is to be read
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell Jashib; the marginal reading of the scribes, followed here, is Jashub, the form in Numbers 26:24.

decisions.choice: The sons of Issachar: ...
decisions.reason: The genealogies keep one list formula: Literal "the sons of X", Balanced "The sons of X: A, B and C", Readable "X had ... sons" or "X's sons were". The Hebrew opens with "and to", which Literal shows as "as for"; Readable folds the number "four" into the sentence.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י תוֹלָ֗ע עֻזִּ֡י וּרְפָיָ֡ה וִֽ֠ירִיאֵל וְיַחְמַ֨י וְיִבְשָׂ֜ם וּשְׁמוּאֵ֗ל רָאשִׁ֤ים לְבֵית־אֲבוֹתָם֙ לְתוֹלָ֔ע גִּבּ֥וֹרֵי חַ֖יִל לְתֹלְדוֹתָ֑ם מִסְפָּרָם֙ בִּימֵ֣י דָוִ֔יד עֶשְׂרִֽים־וּשְׁנַ֥יִם אֶ֖לֶף וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Tola: Uzzi and Rephaiah and Jeriel and Jahmai and Ibsam and Shemuel, heads of [the] house of their fathers, of Tola, mighty [men] of valor by their generations; their number in [the] days of David [was] twenty and two thousand and six hundred.

en.L: And [the] sons of Tola: Uzzi and Rephaiah and Jeriel and Jahmai and Ibsam and Shemuel, heads of the house of their fathers, of Tola, mighty men of valor by their generations; their number in the days of David [was] 22,600.
en.B: The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Shemuel. They were heads of their ancestral families descended from Tola, mighty warriors listed by their generations. In the days of David they numbered 22,600.
en.R: Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Shemuel. They were heads of the families that came from Tola, and they were brave warriors. In David's time, the men in their family lines numbered 22,600.

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: strong, able fighting men
decisions.reason: The phrase joins "mighty man" with a word for strength, ability and wealth. In these lists it names the men of a family fit to fight, as in Joshua 1:14. The same phrase recurs through the chapter (verses 5, 7, 9, 11, 40).

decisions.choice: in the days of David: a count made in David's reign
decisions.reason: David had the fighting men of Israel counted (2 Samuel 24:1-9; 1 Chronicles 21:1-6; 27:23-24). The writer may draw these figures from that count or from records kept in his time.

decisions.choice: twenty-two thousand six hundred: the word read as the number "thousand"
alternatives: twenty-two units with six hundred men
decisions.reason: As in the census lists of Numbers, the word for "thousand" could also name a clan or military unit, which would give much smaller figures; see the note at Numbers 1:21. The same applies to every total in this chapter.

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor / mighty warriors / brave warriors
decisions.reason: One wording for this phrase at each level through the genealogies: Literal "mighty men of valor", Balanced "mighty warriors", Readable "brave warriors".

decisions.choice: Shemuel
decisions.reason: This is the same name as Samuel; it keeps the spelling of the source data so that this man of Issachar is not confused with the prophet.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֥י עֻזִּ֖י יִֽזְרַֽחְיָ֑ה וּבְנֵ֣י יִֽזְרַֽחְיָ֗ה מִֽיכָאֵ֡ל וְ֠עֹבַדְיָה וְיוֹאֵ֧ל יִשִּׁיָּ֛ה חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה רָאשִׁ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah; and [the] sons of Izrahiah: Michael and Obadiah and Joel, Isshiah, five, heads all of them.

en.L: And [the] sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah; and the sons of Izrahiah: Michael and Obadiah and Joel, Isshiah: five, all of them heads.
en.B: The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel and Isshiah. All five of them were chiefs.
en.R: Uzzi's son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah's sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel and Isshiah. These five men were all chiefs.

decisions.choice: five: Izrahiah and his four sons
decisions.reason: Four sons are named, but the total is five. The count most likely includes Izrahiah himself with his sons, all heads of families.

decisions.choice: The son of Uzzi
decisions.reason: The list formula has "sons" even where only one son is named. Balanced and Readable say "son"; Literal keeps "sons".

source.text: וַעֲלֵיהֶ֨ם לְתֹלְדוֹתָ֜ם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבוֹתָ֗ם גְּדוּדֵי֙ צְבָ֣א מִלְחָמָ֔ה שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף כִּֽי־הִרְבּ֥וּ נָשִׁ֖ים וּבָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And with them, by their generations, by [the] house of their fathers, bands of [the] army of war, thirty and six thousand, for they had made many wives and sons.

en.L: And with them, by their generations, by the house of their fathers, [were] bands of the army of war, 36,000, for they had many wives and sons.
en.B: Along with them, by their generations and ancestral families, there were 36,000 troops ready for war, for they had many wives and children.
en.R: Together with these leaders there were 36,000 men in army units ready for war. This was because their families had many wives and children.

decisions.choice: bands of the army of war: fighting units
decisions.reason: The word for "bands" is used of troops or raiding parties (2 Samuel 3:22). Joined with "army of war" it means men organized for battle.

decisions.choice: for they had many wives and sons: the families grew large
decisions.reason: The writer explains the large number by the size of the families. Taking more than one wife was practiced in Israel at the time, and "sons" here means children.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: "Sons" stands for offspring in general here, so Balanced and Readable say "children"; Literal keeps "sons".

source.text: וַאֲחֵיהֶ֗ם לְכֹל֙ מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת יִשָׂשכָ֔ר גִּבּוֹרֵ֖י חֲיָלִ֑ים שְׁמוֹנִ֤ים וְשִׁבְעָה֙ אֶ֔לֶף הִתְיַחְשָׂ֖ם לַכֹּֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And their brothers, of all [the] clans of Issachar, mighty [men] of valor, eighty and seven thousand [was] their enrolling by genealogy for all.

en.L: And their brothers, of all the clans of Issachar, mighty men of valor, 87,000 [was] their enrollment by genealogy, for all.
en.B: Their relatives in all the clans of Issachar were mighty warriors. In all, 87,000 of them were registered in the genealogies.
en.R: Their relatives in all the clans of Issachar were brave warriors. In all, 87,000 men were listed in the family records.

decisions.choice: enrollment by genealogy: registration in the family records
decisions.reason: The verb means to be entered in a genealogical register. Such records counted the men of each family, and here the count is of those able to fight. Chronicles uses the word often (1 Chronicles 4:33; 5:1, 7, 17; 9:1).

decisions.choice: their brothers: their kinsmen
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means the other members of the tribe, all the clans of Issachar.

decisions.choice: enrollment by genealogy / registered in the genealogies / listed in the family records
decisions.reason: One wording for this term at each level through the chapter.

source.text: בִּנְיָמִ֗ן בֶּ֧לַע וָבֶ֛כֶר וִידִֽיעֲאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: Benjamin: Bela and Becher and Jediael, three.

en.L: Benjamin: Bela and Becher and Jediael, three.
en.B: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher and Jediael, three in all.
en.R: Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher and Jediael.

decisions.choice: Bela, Becher and Jediael: a different list of Benjamin's sons
decisions.reason: Genesis 46:21 gives Benjamin ten sons, including Bela and Becher. Numbers 26:38-40 names five clans and has no Becher, and 1 Chronicles 8:1-2 lists Bela, Ashbel, Aharah, Nohah and Rapha. Jediael is named only here. Family lists were drawn up for different purposes and times, as some lines died out and others grew; this one counts the fighting men of three family lines (verses 7-11). Because Zebulun, otherwise missing from these chapters, is not listed, some have thought this section first belonged to Zebulun, but the text as it stands names Benjamin.

decisions.choice: The sons of Benjamin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew starts with the bare name "Benjamin". Balanced and Readable supply "the sons of" to keep the pattern of the list; Literal does not.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י בֶ֗לַע אֶצְבּ֡וֹן וְעֻזִּ֡י וְ֠עֻזִּיאֵל וִירִימ֨וֹת וְעִירִ֜י חֲמִשָּׁ֗ה רָאשֵׁי֙ בֵּ֣ית אָב֔וֹת גִּבּוֹרֵ֖י חֲיָלִ֑ים וְהִתְיַחְשָׂ֗ם עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֨יִם֙ אֶ֔לֶף וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים וְאַרְבָּעָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Bela: Ezbon and Uzzi and Uzziel and Jerimoth and Iri, five, heads of [the] house of fathers, mighty [men] of valor; and their enrolling by genealogy [was] twenty and two thousand and thirty and four.

en.L: And [the] sons of Bela: Ezbon and Uzzi and Uzziel and Jerimoth and Iri, five, heads of the house of fathers, mighty men of valor; and their enrollment by genealogy [was] 22,034.
en.B: The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth and Iri, five in all. They were heads of ancestral families, mighty warriors, and 22,034 were registered in their genealogies.
en.R: Bela had five sons: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth and Iri. They were heads of families and brave warriors. Their family records listed 22,034 men.

decisions.choice: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth and Iri: Bela's sons in this list
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 8:3-5 gives Bela other sons (Addar, Gera, Abihud and others), and Numbers 26:40 names Ard and Naaman. An Ezbon also appears among the sons of Gad (Genesis 46:16). Different lists record different stages or branches of the family.

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor / mighty warriors / brave warriors
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י בֶ֗כֶר זְמִירָ֡ה וְיוֹעָ֡שׁ וֶ֠אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְאֶלְיוֹעֵינַ֤י וְעָמְרִי֙ וִירֵמ֣וֹת וַאֲבִיָּ֔ה וַעֲנָת֖וֹת וְעָלָ֑מֶת כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵי־בָֽכֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Becher: Zemirah and Joash and Eliezer and Elioenai and Omri and Jeremoth and Abijah and Anathoth and Alemeth; all these [were the] sons of Becher.

en.L: And [the] sons of Becher: Zemirah and Joash and Eliezer and Elioenai and Omri and Jeremoth and Abijah and Anathoth and Alemeth; all these [were] the sons of Becher.
en.B: The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Becher.
en.R: Becher's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth. All these were his sons.

decisions.choice: Anathoth and Alemeth: also the names of towns of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Anathoth and Alemeth (or Almon) were Levite towns in Benjamin's land (Joshua 21:18; 1 Chronicles 6:45). The towns may have been named after these men, or the founders of towns may be listed as sons, as often in these genealogies (2:50-55).

source.text: וְהִתְיַחְשָׂ֣ם לְתֹלְדוֹתָ֗ם רָאשֵׁי֙ בֵּ֣ית אֲבוֹתָ֔ם גִּבּוֹרֵ֖י חָ֑יִל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וּמָאתָֽיִם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And their enrolling by genealogy, by their generations, heads of [the] house of their fathers, mighty [men] of valor: twenty thousand and two hundred.

en.L: And their enrollment by genealogy, by their generations, heads of the house of their fathers, mighty men of valor: 20,200.
en.B: Registered in their genealogies by their generations, as heads of their ancestral families, were 20,200 mighty warriors.
en.R: Their family records listed the heads of their families and 20,200 brave warriors.

decisions.choice: the total for Becher's family
decisions.reason: The heads of families and the fighting men of Becher's line are counted together in one total, as in verse 7.

decisions.choice: listed the heads of their families and 20,200 brave warriors
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the Hebrew's two parts, the heads of families and the warriors, in one simple sentence. The number covers the whole register.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֥י יְדִיעֲאֵ֖ל בִּלְהָ֑ן וּבְנֵ֣י בִלְהָ֗ן יְע֡וּשׁ וּ֠בִנְיָמִן וְאֵה֤וּד וּֽכְנַעֲנָה֙ וְזֵיתָ֔ן וְתַרְשִׁ֖ישׁ וַאֲחִישָֽׁחַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Jediael: Bilhan; and [the] sons of Bilhan: Jeush and Benjamin and Ehud and Chenaanah and Zethan and Tarshish and Ahishahar.

en.L: And [the] sons of Jediael: Bilhan; and the sons of Bilhan: Jeush and Benjamin and Ehud and Chenaanah and Zethan and Tarshish and Ahishahar.
en.B: The son of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar.
en.R: Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar.

decisions.choice: Jeush, as the Hebrew text is to be read
decisions.reason: The written consonants spell Jeish; the scribes' marginal reading, followed here, is Jeush, a name found elsewhere (Genesis 36:5; 1 Chronicles 8:39).

decisions.choice: Benjamin and Ehud: later men with the names of the patriarch and the judge
decisions.reason: This Benjamin is a great-grandson of the tribe's founder, who bears his name. This Ehud is not the judge Ehud son of Gera (Judges 3:15), as far as the text says.

source.text: כָּל־אֵ֜לֶּה בְּנֵ֤י יְדִֽיעֲאֵל֙ לְרָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֔וֹת גִּבּוֹרֵ֖י חֲיָלִ֑ים שִׁבְעָֽה־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֨לֶף֙ וּמָאתַ֔יִם יֹצְאֵ֥י צָבָ֖א לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: All these [were the] sons of Jediael, by heads of the fathers, mighty [men] of valor, seventeen thousand and two hundred, going out [in the] army for battle.

en.L: All these [were] the sons of Jediael, by heads of the fathers, mighty men of valor, 17,200, going out [in the] army for battle.
en.B: All these were sons of Jediael, listed by the heads of their families: 17,200 mighty warriors ready to go out to war.
en.R: All these were Jediael's descendants. Listed by family heads, there were 17,200 brave warriors ready to go out to war.

decisions.choice: going out in the army for battle: men fit for military service
decisions.reason: The phrase describes men able to march out to war, as in the census of Numbers 1:3. The count here covers Jediael's descendants.

decisions.choice: ready to go out to war
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the phrase as "ready to go out to war"; Literal keeps "going out [in the] army for battle".

source.text: וְשֻׁפִּ֤ם וְחֻפִּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י עִ֔יר חֻשִׁ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י אַחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Shuppim and Huppim, [the] sons of Ir; Hushim, [the] sons of Aher.

en.L: And Shuppim and Huppim [were] the sons of Ir; Hushim, the sons of Aher.
en.B: Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir, and Hushim was the son of Aher.
en.R: Shuppim and Huppim were Ir's sons. Hushim was Aher's son.

decisions.choice: Shuppim, Huppim, Ir, Hushim and Aher: names hard to place
decisions.reason: Ir may be Iri, Bela's son (verse 7). Shuppim and Huppim recall Muppim and Huppim in Genesis 46:21 and Shephupham and Hupham in Numbers 26:39. Hushim is the son of Dan in Genesis 46:23, and Aher means "another". The tribe of Dan is not otherwise listed in this chapter, so this half of the verse may once have spoken of Dan; but as the text stands Hushim is the son of a man named Aher.

decisions.choice: the son of Aher
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the list says "sons" for one name; Balanced and Readable say "son".

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י נַפְתָּלִ֗י יַחֲצִיאֵ֧ל וְגוּנִ֛י וְיֵ֥צֶר וְשַׁלּ֖וּם בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Naphtali: Jahziel and Guni and Jezer and Shallum, [the] sons of Bilhah.

en.L: [The] sons of Naphtali: Jahziel and Guni and Jezer and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah.
en.B: The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer and Shallum. These were descendants of Bilhah.
en.R: Naphtali's sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer and Shallum. They were descendants of Bilhah.

decisions.choice: Jahziel and Shallum: the forms of Jahzeel and Shillem in Genesis 46:24
decisions.reason: Genesis 46:24 and Numbers 26:48-49 spell the first and last sons Jahzeel and Shillem. These are different spellings of the same names.

decisions.choice: the sons of Bilhah: descended from Bilhah
decisions.reason: Bilhah was Rachel's servant, who bore Dan and Naphtali to Jacob (Genesis 30:3-8). Naphtali's sons are her grandsons, listed under her name as in Genesis 46:25.

decisions.choice: descendants of Bilhah
decisions.reason: Bilhah is their grandmother, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants"; Literal keeps "sons".

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה אַשְׂרִיאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָלָ֑דָה פִּֽילַגְשׁוֹ֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּיָּ֔ה יָלְדָ֕ה אֶת־מָכִ֖יר אֲבִ֥י גִלְעָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom she bore; his concubine the Aramean bore Machir [the] father of Gilead.

en.L: [The] sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom she bore; his concubine, the Aramean woman, bore Machir the father of Gilead.
en.B: The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his wife bore, and Machir the father of Gilead, whom his Aramean concubine bore.
en.R: Manasseh's sons were Asriel and Machir. Machir's mother was Manasseh's concubine (a secondary wife), a woman from Aram. Machir was the father of Gilead.

decisions.choice: Asriel, whom she bore: the mother is not named
alternatives: Asriel, whom his wife bore (supplying the missing subject)
decisions.reason: The verb "she bore" has no subject, so a woman's name or "his wife" seems to have dropped out of the text. Asriel is a clan of Gilead's line in Numbers 26:31 and Joshua 17:2, so here a later clan may be counted as a son of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: his Aramean concubine bore Machir the father of Gilead
decisions.reason: Machir is Manasseh's son in Genesis 50:23 and Numbers 26:29. Only this verse says that his mother was an Aramean concubine, a secondary wife from the people of Aram to the north and east.

decisions.choice: whom his wife bore
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "his wife" so that the clause has a subject; Literal keeps the bare "whom she bore", and Readable names both sons without saying who bore Asriel.

decisions.choice: concubine (a secondary wife)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "concubine" at its first use in the chapter, as in Judges.

source.text: וּמָכִ֞יר לָקַ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לְחֻפִּ֣ים וּלְשֻׁפִּ֔ים וְשֵׁ֤ם אֲחֹתוֹ֙ מַעֲכָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖י צְלָפְחָ֑ד וַתִּהְיֶ֥נָה לִצְלָפְחָ֖ד בָּנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And Machir took a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim, and [the] name of his sister [was] Maacah; and [the] name of the second [was] Zelophehad; and there were to Zelophehad daughters.

en.L: And Machir took a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim, and the name of his sister [was] Maacah. And the name of the second [was] Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.
en.B: Machir took a wife for Huppim and Shuppim, and his sister's name was Maacah. The second was named Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.
en.R: Machir found a wife for Huppim and Shuppim. His sister's name was Maacah. The second son was named Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had only daughters.

decisions.choice: a wife for Huppim and Shuppim ... his sister Maacah ... the second: the text is hard to follow
alternatives: Machir took a wife whose name was Maacah (a common suggestion for restoring the verse)
decisions.reason: The verse does not hang together as it stands. Huppim and Shuppim are Benjamin's line (verse 12), Maacah is Machir's wife in verse 16 but "his sister" here, and "the second" has no first named before it. Words have probably dropped out. The text is translated as it stands.

decisions.choice: Zelophehad had daughters: the daughters of Numbers 26-27
decisions.reason: Zelophehad, of Manasseh's line, had no sons, and his daughters asked Moses for their father's share of the land (Numbers 26:33; 27:1-11; 36:1-12; Joshua 17:3-6). Numbers makes him the son of Hepher, four generations from Manasseh; this verse only calls him "the second".

decisions.choice: The second son ... had only daughters
decisions.reason: Readable supplies "son" for "the second" and "only" from Numbers 26:33, which says he had no sons. "The second" is a man's form in the Hebrew.

source.text: וַתֵּ֨לֶד מַעֲכָ֤ה אֵֽשֶׁת־מָכִיר֙ בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ פֶּ֔רֶשׁ וְשֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו שָׁ֑רֶשׁ וּבָנָ֖יו אוּלָ֥ם וָרָֽקֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And bore Maacah, [the] wife of Machir, a son, and she called his name Peresh; and [the] name of his brother [was] Sheresh; and his sons [were] Ulam and Rekem.

en.L: And Maacah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she called his name Peresh; and the name of his brother [was] Sheresh; and his sons [were] Ulam and Rekem.
en.B: Maacah, the wife of Machir, gave birth to a son, and she named him Peresh. His brother's name was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rekem.
en.R: Machir's wife Maacah had a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh. Sheresh had two sons, Ulam and Rekem.

decisions.choice: his sons: probably Sheresh's
decisions.reason: "His sons" most naturally belongs to the last man named, Sheresh, though it could be Peresh's.

decisions.choice: Sheresh had two sons
decisions.reason: Readable names Sheresh as the father, the nearer reading; the meaning decision (m1) notes the other.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֥י אוּלָ֖ם בְּדָ֑ן אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד בֶּן־מָכִ֖יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Ulam: Bedan. These [were the] sons of Gilead [the] son of Machir [the] son of Manasseh.

en.L: And [the] sons of Ulam: Bedan. These [were] the sons of Gilead the son of Machir the son of Manasseh.
en.B: The son of Ulam: Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh.
en.R: Ulam's son was Bedan. All these were descendants of Gilead, the son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: the sons of Gilead: the families of Gilead's line
decisions.reason: "Sons" here sums up the line from verses 14-17 as Gilead's descendants. Gilead was Machir's son (Numbers 26:29), so the list traces Manasseh's tribe through Machir and Gilead.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "descendants" where the word sums up more than one generation; Literal keeps "sons".

source.text: וַאֲחֹת֖וֹ הַמֹּלֶ֑כֶת יָלְדָה֙ אֶת־אִישְׁה֔וֹד וְאֶת־אֲבִיעֶ֖זֶר וְאֶת־מַחְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And his sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod and Abiezer and Mahlah.

en.L: And his sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod and Abiezer and Mahlah.
en.B: His sister Hammolecheth gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer and Mahlah.
en.R: Gilead's sister Hammolecheth had three children: Ishhod, Abiezer and Mahlah.

decisions.choice: his sister: Gilead's sister
decisions.reason: "His" points back to the last main name in verse 17, Gilead, the son of Machir.

decisions.choice: Abiezer: the clan of Gideon
decisions.reason: Abiezer is the first of Manasseh's clans in Joshua 17:2 (Iezer in Numbers 26:30), and Gideon came from the Abiezrites (Judges 6:11). Mahlah is also the name of one of Zelophehad's daughters (Numbers 26:33); here it may be a son or a daughter.

decisions.choice: Gilead's sister ... three children
decisions.reason: Readable names Gilead for "his" and says "children", since Mahlah may be a woman.

source.text: וַיִּהְי֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י שְׁמִידָ֑ע אַחְיָ֣ן וָשֶׁ֔כֶם וְלִקְחִ֖י וַאֲנִיעָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And were [the] sons of Shemida: Ahian and Shechem and Likhi and Aniam.

en.L: And [the] sons of Shemida were Ahian and Shechem and Likhi and Aniam.
en.B: The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi and Aniam.
en.R: Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi and Aniam.

decisions.choice: Shemida and Shechem: clans of Gilead's line
decisions.reason: Shemida and Shechem are both clans of Gilead in Numbers 26:31-32 and Joshua 17:2. Here Shechem is listed as Shemida's son.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֥י אֶפְרַ֖יִם שׁוּתָ֑לַח וּבֶ֤רֶד בְּנוֹ֙ וְתַ֣חַת בְּנ֔וֹ וְאֶלְעָדָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ וְתַ֥חַת בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eleadah his son, and Tahath his son,

en.L: And [the] sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eleadah his son, and Tahath his son,
en.B: The descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
en.R: These were Ephraim's descendants: Shuthelah, then his son Bered, then Bered's son Tahath, then Tahath's son Eleadah, then Eleadah's son Tahath,

decisions.choice: Shuthelah: the first clan of Ephraim
decisions.reason: Shuthelah heads Ephraim's clans in Numbers 26:35. Tahath may be the same as Tahan there; a Tahan appears again in verse 25. The list here runs from father to son through several generations.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: The list goes down several generations, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants". Readable spells out each step ("then his son") so a reader can follow the line.

source.text: וְזָבָ֥ד בְּנ֛וֹ וְשׁוּתֶ֥לַח בְּנ֖וֹ וְעֵ֣זֶר וְאֶלְעָ֑ד וַהֲרָג֗וּם אַנְשֵׁי־גַת֙ הַנּוֹלָדִ֣ים בָּאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֣י יָרְד֔וּ לָקַ֖חַת אֶת־מִקְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead; and killed them [the] men of Gath, the [ones] born in the land, because they went down to take their livestock.

en.L: and Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead. And the men of Gath, who were born in the land, killed them, because they went down to take their livestock.
en.B: Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, and also Ezer and Elead. The men of Gath who were born in that land killed Ezer and Elead, because they went down to take their livestock.
en.R: then Tahath's son Zabad, then Zabad's son Shuthelah. Ephraim also had sons named Ezer and Elead. They were killed by the men of Gath, the people native to that land, because they went down to take their livestock.

decisions.choice: Ezer and Elead: Ephraim's own sons
decisions.reason: The line "his son ... his son" stops with Shuthelah. Ezer and Elead are then named without "his son", and verse 22 calls Ephraim "their father", so they were Ephraim's own sons.

decisions.choice: they went down to take their livestock: Ephraim's sons raiding Gath
alternatives: the men of Gath came down to take the Ephraimites' livestock
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say whose livestock or who went down. "Went down" suits men going from the hill country of Ephraim down to Gath in the lowland, and "born in the land" describes the people of Gath as natives defending their own herds. So Ezer and Elead most likely raided Gath's livestock and were killed. It is also possible that the men of Gath came down to take Ephraim's livestock and killed his sons.

decisions.choice: the men of Gath born in the land: the native people of the city
decisions.reason: Gath was later a Philistine city (1 Samuel 17:4), but "born in the land" points to the people who lived there before. The story is set in Ephraim's lifetime, though Genesis places Ephraim in Egypt (Genesis 41:52; 50:23); the text does not explain when or how the raid took place.

decisions.choice: killed Ezer and Elead / They were killed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Ezer and Elead as the men killed, as m1 explains. Like Literal, they leave open whose livestock it was.

source.text: וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֛ל אֶפְרַ֥יִם אֲבִיהֶ֖ם יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶחָ֖יו לְנַחֲמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And mourned Ephraim their father many days, and came his brothers to comfort him.

en.L: And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
en.B: Ephraim their father mourned for many days, and his relatives came to console him.
en.R: Their father Ephraim grieved for them a long time. His relatives came to comfort him.

decisions.choice: mourned many days ... came to comfort him: an echo of Jacob's grief for Joseph
decisions.reason: Jacob mourned for his son Joseph "many days", and his family rose to comfort him (Genesis 37:34-35). Ephraim, Joseph's son, grieves in the same words for his own sons.

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: "Brothers" means his kin, the wider family; Balanced and Readable say "relatives".

source.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶת־שְׁמוֹ֙ בְּרִיעָ֔ה כִּ֥י בְרָעָ֖ה הָיְתָ֥ה בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Beriah, because in disaster it was in his house.

en.L: And he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it was in disaster in his house.
en.B: Then he lay with his wife, and she became pregnant and bore a son. He named him Beriah, because disaster had come upon his family.
en.R: Later Ephraim slept with his wife, and she became pregnant and had a son. He named him Beriah, which sounds like the Hebrew words for "in disaster". He chose this name because trouble had come to his family.

decisions.choice: Beriah: a name that sounds like "in disaster"
decisions.reason: The name Beriah sounds like the phrase be-ra'ah, "in disaster" or "in misfortune". The name keeps the memory of the sons who were killed (verse 21). Names given for the circumstances of a birth are common in Genesis (Genesis 35:18). Others named Beriah are in verse 30 and 8:13.

decisions.choice: it was in disaster in his house: the family's misfortune
alternatives: because she was in misfortune in his house
decisions.reason: The verb "it was" is feminine and may refer to the event, the family's state, or the child's birth taking place in a time of trouble. The sense is the same: the son was born while the household was in mourning.

decisions.choice: went in to his wife: had sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: The phrase is the ordinary way of saying a man slept with his wife (Genesis 29:23; 30:4).

decisions.choice: which sounds like the Hebrew words for "in disaster"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the play on words in the text itself, so that the reason for the name is clear; Literal and Balanced leave it to the footnote (m1).

source.text: וּבִתּ֣וֹ שֶׁאֱרָ֔ה וַתִּ֧בֶן אֶת־בֵּית־חוֹר֛וֹן הַתַּחְתּ֖וֹן וְאֶת־הָעֶלְי֑וֹן וְאֵ֖ת אֻזֵּ֥ן שֶׁאֱרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And his daughter [was] Sheerah, and she built Beth-horon the lower and the upper, and Uzzen-sheerah.

en.L: And his daughter [was] Sheerah, and she built Lower and Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sheerah.
en.B: His daughter was Sheerah. She built Lower and Upper Beth-horon, and also Uzzen-sheerah.
en.R: His daughter was Sheerah. She built the towns of Lower Beth-horon and Upper Beth-horon, and also Uzzen-sheerah.

decisions.choice: built: founded or fortified
decisions.reason: The verb "build" is used both for founding a town and for rebuilding or fortifying one (1 Kings 9:17). Sheerah is remembered as the builder of these towns, a rare record of a woman doing so.

decisions.choice: Lower and Upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sheerah
decisions.reason: The two Beth-horons stood on the border of Ephraim's land (Joshua 16:3, 5). Uzzen-sheerah is not mentioned anywhere else; its name contains Sheerah's own.

decisions.choice: his daughter: Ephraim's or Beriah's
decisions.reason: "His" may refer to Ephraim, the main figure of verses 22-23, or to Beriah, the last man named. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: the towns of
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the towns of" so the names are understood as places.

source.text: וְרֶ֣פַח בְּנ֗וֹ וְרֶ֧שֶׁף וְתֶ֛לַח בְּנ֖וֹ וְתַ֥חַן בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Rephah his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, and Tahan his son,

en.L: And Rephah [was] his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, and Tahan his son,
en.B: Rephah was his son, and also Resheph; then Telah his son, Tahan his son,
en.R: Rephah was his son, and so was Resheph. Next in the line came Telah his son, Tahan his son,

decisions.choice: Rephah his son: the line of Joshua resumes
decisions.reason: The list picks up again after the story of Beriah. "His son" probably means a son of Ephraim, or of Beriah, and from Telah on the line runs from father to son down to Joshua (verse 27).

decisions.choice: Next in the line came
decisions.reason: Readable adds "next in the line came" to show that the list continues from generation to generation.

source.text: לַעְדָּ֥ן בְּנ֛וֹ עַמִּיה֥וּד בְּנ֖וֹ אֱלִישָׁמָ֥ע בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,

en.L: Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
en.B: Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
en.R: Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,

decisions.choice: Elishama son of Ammihud: the leader of Ephraim in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Elishama son of Ammihud led the tribe of Ephraim when Israel was counted and camped in the wilderness (Numbers 1:10; 2:18; 7:48).

source.text: נ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Nun his son, Joshua his son.

en.L: Nun his son, Joshua his son.
en.B: Nun his son and Joshua his son.
en.R: Nun his son, and Joshua his son.

decisions.choice: Nun his son, Joshua his son: Joshua son of Nun
decisions.reason: The line of Ephraim ends with Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant and successor, who led Israel into the land (Numbers 13:8, 16; Joshua 1:1). Only this list traces his ancestry back to Ephraim. The family that grieved in verse 22 thus leads to the man who brought Israel into its inheritance.

source.text: וַאֲחֻזָּתָם֙ וּמֹ֣שְׁבוֹתָ֔ם בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל וּבְנֹתֶ֑יהָ וְלַמִּזְרָ֣ח נַעֲרָ֔ן וְלַֽמַּעֲרָ֗ב גֶּ֤זֶר וּבְנֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ וּשְׁכֶ֣ם וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ עַד־עַיָּ֖ה וּבְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And their possession and their dwellings [were] Bethel and its daughters, and to the east Naaran, and to the west Gezer and its daughters, and Shechem and its daughters as far as Ayyah and its daughters;

en.L: And their possession and their dwellings [were] Bethel and its villages, and to the east Naaran, and to the west Gezer and its villages, and Shechem and its villages, as far as Ayyah and its villages;
en.B: Their land and settlements were Bethel with its villages, Naaran on the east, Gezer with its villages on the west, and Shechem with its villages as far as Ayyah with its villages.
en.R: The land where Ephraim's people lived included Bethel and the villages around it. It reached Naaran on the east and Gezer and its villages on the west. It also included Shechem and its villages, as far as Ayyah and its villages.

decisions.choice: its daughters: its villages
decisions.reason: "Daughters" of a town are the smaller settlements that depend on it, as in Numbers 21:25 and Joshua 17:11.

decisions.choice: Bethel, Naaran, Gezer, Shechem and Ayyah: the bounds of Ephraim
decisions.reason: These places mark the land of Ephraim as in Joshua 16:1-10, where Naaran is called Naarah (Joshua 16:7). Ayyah is perhaps the same as Ai (Joshua 7:2); some Hebrew manuscripts read Gaza here, which lies far to the southwest.

decisions.choice: villages
decisions.reason: As in Joshua 17:11, "daughters" is given as "villages" at every level; the gloss keeps "daughters".

source.text: וְעַל־יְדֵ֣י בְנֵי־מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה בֵּית־שְׁאָ֤ן וּבְנֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ תַּעְנַ֣ךְ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ מְגִדּ֥וֹ וּבְנוֹתֶ֖יהָ דּ֣וֹר וּבְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ בְּאֵ֨לֶּה֙ יָשְׁב֔וּ בְּנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֖ף בֶּן־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and on [the] hands of [the] sons of Manasseh: Beth-shean and its daughters, Taanach and its daughters, Megiddo and its daughters, Dor and its daughters. In these dwelt [the] sons of Joseph son of Israel.

en.L: and along the hands of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Manasseh, Beth-shean and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, Dor and its villages. In these lived the {{gender:children|sons}} of Joseph the son of Israel.
en.B: Along the borders of the descendants of Manasseh were Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo and Dor, each with its villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel made their homes in these towns.
en.R: Next to the land of the tribe of Manasseh were Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo and Dor, with the villages around each town. The descendants of Joseph, the son of Israel, lived in these places.

decisions.choice: on the hands of: alongside, in the region of
decisions.reason: "Hands" here means the sides or borders of a territory. These towns lay in or beside Manasseh's area west of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo, Dor: Manasseh's towns, as in Joshua 17:11
decisions.reason: Joshua 17:11 gives these towns to Manasseh though they lay in the lands of Issachar and Asher, and Joshua 17:12 and Judges 1:27 say Manasseh could not at first drive out the Canaanites from them. The summary "the sons of Joseph" joins Ephraim and Manasseh, Joseph's two sons.

decisions.choice: the {{gender:children|sons}} of / the descendants of
decisions.reason: Here "sons of" names a whole tribe, men and women, so Literal uses the gender setting and Balanced and Readable say "descendants", as Joshua 16:5 does for Ephraim.

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י אָשֵׁ֗ר יִמְנָ֧ה וְיִשְׁוָ֛ה וְיִשְׁוִ֥י וּבְרִיעָ֖ה וְשֶׂ֥רַח אֲחוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Asher: Imnah and Ishvah and Ishvi and Beriah, and Serah their sister.

en.L: [The] sons of Asher: Imnah and Ishvah and Ishvi and Beriah, and Serah their sister.
en.B: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah, and their sister Serah.
en.R: Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.

decisions.choice: Asher's four sons and his daughter Serah, as in Genesis 46:17
decisions.reason: The names match Genesis 46:17 exactly. Numbers 26:44-46 lists clans from Imnah, Ishvi and Beriah, and names Serah too.

decisions.choice: Their sister was Serah.
decisions.reason: As in Genesis 46:17, Readable gives the sister a sentence of her own.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י בְרִיעָ֔ה חֶ֖בֶר וּמַלְכִּיאֵ֑ל ה֖וּא אֲבִ֥י בִרְזָֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel; he [was the] father of Birzaith.

en.L: And [the] sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel; he [was] the father of Birzaith.
en.B: The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
en.R: Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel. Malchiel was the father of Birzaith.

decisions.choice: Birzaith, as the Hebrew text is to be read
decisions.reason: The written consonants suggest Birzavith; the scribes' marginal reading, followed here, is Birzaith.

decisions.choice: father of Birzaith: perhaps the founder of a town
decisions.reason: Birzaith may be a place, and "father" can mean the founder or leading man of a town, as often in these lists (2:50-52; 4:4).

decisions.choice: Malchiel was
decisions.reason: Readable names Malchiel for "he", the nearest name.

source.text: וְחֶ֨בֶר֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־יַפְלֵ֔ט וְאֶת־שׁוֹמֵ֖ר וְאֶת־חוֹתָ֑ם וְאֵ֖ת שׁוּעָ֥א אֲחוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Heber fathered Japhlet and Shomer and Hotham, and Shua their sister.

en.L: And Heber begot Japhlet and Shomer and Hotham, and Shua their sister.
en.B: Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer and Hotham, and of their sister Shua.
en.R: Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer and Hotham. Their sister was Shua.

decisions.choice: fathered: became the father of
decisions.reason: The verb is the form used for a father in family lists (Genesis 5:3-32).

decisions.choice: begot / was the father of
decisions.reason: The genealogies use one wording: Literal "begot", Balanced and Readable "was the father of".

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יַפְלֵ֔ט פָּסַ֥ךְ וּבִמְהָ֖ל וְעַשְׁוָ֑ת אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י יַפְלֵֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Japhlet: Pasach and Bimhal and Ashvath; these [were the] sons of Japhlet.

en.L: And [the] sons of Japhlet: Pasach and Bimhal and Ashvath; these [were] the sons of Japhlet.
en.B: The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal and Ashvath. These were the sons of Japhlet.
en.R: Japhlet's sons were Pasach, Bimhal and Ashvath. These were Japhlet's sons.

decisions.choice: Japhlet: perhaps linked with the Japhletites
decisions.reason: A clan called the Japhletites gave its name to an area on Ephraim's border (Joshua 16:3). It may be connected with this Japhlet of Asher, but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: Shemer: the Shomer of verse 32
decisions.reason: Shemer is another spelling of Shomer, Heber's son (verse 32).

decisions.choice: Ahi and Rohgah and Hubbah, as the Hebrew text is to be read
alternatives: the sons of Shemer his brother: Rohgah, Jehubbah and Aram
decisions.reason: The written consonants give "and Rohgah, Jehubbah"; the scribes' marginal reading, followed here, has "and Rohgah and Hubbah". "Ahi" could also be read "his brother", which would give "the sons of Shemer his brother: Rohgah ..." and match "Helem his brother" in verse 35.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "son" before a list of four, using the singular for the whole family; Balanced and Readable say "sons".

records.literal_gloss: All these [were the] sons of Asher, heads of [the] house of the fathers, chosen [men], mighty [men] of valor, heads of the leaders; and their enrolling by genealogy in the army in battle, their number [was] men twenty and six thousand.

en.L: All these [were] the sons of Asher, heads of the house of the fathers, chosen men, mighty men of valor, heads of the leaders. And their enrollment by genealogy in the army for battle: their number [was] 26,000 men.
en.B: All these were descendants of Asher, heads of ancestral families, choice men, mighty warriors, chief among the leaders. The number of men registered in their genealogies for service in war was 26,000.
en.R: All these were Asher's descendants. They were heads of families, the best of men and brave warriors, the chief leaders. The men listed in their family records as able to fight in the army numbered 26,000.

decisions.choice: chosen: picked, the best
decisions.reason: The word means purified or selected, and describes men of proven quality (1 Chronicles 9:22; 16:41).

decisions.choice: heads of the leaders: the foremost leaders
decisions.reason: The phrase sets these men at the top of the tribe's leaders. The word for "leaders" is the one used for tribal leaders in Numbers (Numbers 1:16).

decisions.choice: twenty-six thousand: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: On the size of the totals, see verse 2 and Numbers 1:21.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, "sons" sums up several generations, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants".
